title: Deterministic credit aggregation for out-of-order/late streaming fragments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
We observe persistent discrepancies between tokens billed and tokens produced for long-lived streaming sessions under intermittent network conditions. Root cause analysis shows the metering pipeline performs multi-stage aggregation (edge ingestion -> gateway aggregator -> billing ledger) and uses non-deterministic windowing + best-effort dedupe, which fails for out-of-order fragments, resumed sessions with new session IDs, and mid-stream model switches. Consequences include both underbilling (missing late fragments) and double billing (retry + incomplete dedupe), customer charge variance, and rate limiter mis-accounting leading to premature throttles or invisible overages.

Reproduction notes:
- Simulated flaky mobile client that retransmits suffix fragments with different stream resume ids while the gateway performs partial prefix caching.
- Observed cases where fragment A arrives after fragment B (A.seq < B.seq) and aggregator attributes both to distinct logical outputs because session_id changed on resume.
- Replayed historical traces: ~0.18% of streams in the last 30 days had evidence of out-of-order fragments that increased accounting variance beyond the 99.9% target.

Goals:
1) Ensure deterministic, idempotent attribution of input/output token credits for any fragment order, retries, and model switch fallbacks.
2) Keep added latency and write amplification minimal (target <1% p99 latency regressions for gateway paths).
3) Provide reconciliation tooling and metrics so misses/duplicates are visible and automatically fixed when possible.

Proposed solution (high-level):
- Introduce a stable chunk identifier (metering_chunk_id) generated by the serving runtime for every fragment: sha256(request_uuid + fragment_seq + fragment_nonce). This travels with every streaming fragment and any resume/ retry.
- Change aggregation semantics: gateway aggregator will not rely solely on session_id; it will aggregate per request_uuid and per metering_chunk_id. Aggregator keeps a small write-through cache of seen chunk ids (TTL: 24h) and emits exactly-once delta events to billing ledger.
- Add a finalization signal: when the runtime completes a response (or performs a guaranteed fallback to another model), it emits a terminal event (metering_finalize) with a compact manifest of chunk ids and final model tag. Billing pipeline uses this as authoritative reconciliation.
- Ledger writes will be idempotent: billing_ingest service will use chunk_id as the dedupe key; duplicate attempts are ignored. For partial fragments that later complete (e.g., resumed with additional tokens), finalization will cause a reconcile flow that updates the billed token count to the final sum.
- Implement a background Reconciliation job that 1) scans un-finalized requests older than X minutes, 2) queries serving trace/logs for late arrivals, and 3) emits corrective adjustments (delta credits) to the ledger with metadata.

Schema changes (backwards-compatible):
- metering_event: add fields metering_chunk_id (string), request_uuid (string), chunk_seq (int as string), finalized (bool as string), origin_model (string), resume_hint (string). All fields optional for older clients; default path preserves current behavior.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Pros: deterministic dedupe, clear reconciliation path, fewer charge disputes.
- Cons: additional metadata increases event size (approx +120 bytes per fragment), small extra writes for aggregator cache and finalization events, complexity in rollout across Dedicated/Private customers.
- Risk mitigation: feature will be rollout behind a feature flag, initially enabled only for hosted API and a small dedicated canary pool.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (week 0-1): Runtime change to emit metering_chunk_id and request_uuid with every fragment; gateway aggregator accepts the new fields but preserves old logic if fields absent. Add unit tests and schema compatibility tests.
Phase 2 (week 1-2): Billing_ingest idempotency by chunk_id; local e2e test harness; add aggregator write-through cache (in-memory with Redis fallback).
Phase 3 (week 2-3): Finalization event implementation; reconciliation job and corrective delta writes; dashboards and alerts.
Phase 4 (week 3-4): Canary rollout (5% of hosted traffic), increased to 25% after monitoring OK, full rollout to hosted. Dedicated/private customers will be given a migration guide and opt-in flag.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for chunk id generation, dedupe logic, and finalize semantics.
- Integration tests using the streaming simulator that fuzzes reorder, drops, and resume with new session ids. Create property-based tests comparing ledger outcomes against a ground-truth simulator.
- Load test to verify aggregator cache and idempotency behavior at peak throughput (target: sustain current QPS with <3% CPU increase on aggregator).
- E2E billing reconciliation run on replay of last 7 days of production events in staging to verify corrective delta volumes are within expected bounds.

Monitoring and metrics:
- New metrics: metering.chunk_late_arrival_rate, metering.dedupe_hits, metering.reconciliation_adjustments_total, metering.finalize_missing_rate.
- Alert: reconcile_adjustments_total > 0.1% of billed tokens in a 1h window -> pager to SRE/Payments.

Rollout & rollback:
- Feature flags: metering_chunk_ids_enabled (runtime), aggregator_strict_mode (billing).
- Canary 5% hosted traffic -> monitor metrics for 48h -> escalate to 25% if no regressions -> 100% hosted.
- Rollback path: flip feature flag off; reconciliation job should be idempotent and safe to stop. Billing ledger accepts both old and new schemas so no hard failure expected.

Open questions / decisions required:
- TTL for aggregator seen-chunk cache: 24h recommended but needs cost estimate from infra (storage + eviction load).
- Whether to backfill chunk ids for past requests for more accurate reconciliation (expensive).
- Exact format for request_uuid (use existing trace id or new uuid?). Prefer using the existing request trace id to avoid cross-service correlation gaps.

Stakeholders and reviewers:

- Serving runtime: Daniel Park (chunk id generation)
- Gateway/ingest: Miguel Ortega (assignee)
- SRE: Tomasz Nowak (deployment/canary)
- Legal/Finance: Clara Liu (billing dispute policy)

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MET/Deterministic+Chunk+Attribution (draft)
- E2E simulator harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-sim
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1428 (runtime chunk id), https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/659 (accept chunk id), https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/321 (idempotent ledger write)

Expected outcome:
- Reduce customer-facing billing variance attributable to streaming fragments by >95% in production within 2 weeks of full rollout.
- Reduce billing disputes tied to late-arrival/dedup issues by 90% over 60 days.

Longer-term follow-ups (not in scope for this ticket):
- Explore compact bloom-filter-based dedupe for ultra-high-throughput customers to reduce cache footprint.
- Expose per-request metering manifest to customers via the Console for auditability.
